title: Peristaltic Pump

introduction.definition: A peristaltic (hose) pump moves liquid by squeezing a flexible hose or tube with rollers or shoes on a rotor. The occlusion travels along the hose, pushing the liquid ahead of it; the hose recovers its shape behind the shoe and draws in more liquid. The liquid touches only the hose.
applications: Mining and alumina: thickener underflow sampling, reagent dosing
key_points: Only the hose is wetted — no seals or valves
Can run dry; self-priming to high suction lift
Hose life is the main cost

classification.configuration: Hose pump with two pressing shoes, lubricant-filled housing

introduction.summary: The liquid is enclosed in a flexible hose laid around the inside of the pump housing. Rotating shoes (or rollers) squeeze the hose completely shut and roll the closed point along, pushing the liquid ahead of them; behind the shoe the hose springs back open and draws in more liquid. Only the hose touches the product, there are no seals or valves, and the pump can run dry, self-prime and handle abrasive, viscous and shear-sensitive fluids.

piping: Flexible connections; pulsation dampeners on long lines.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
commissioning: Check lubricant level; check hose installation and shimming.

lubrication: Hose lubricant in housing; gearbox oil.

causes: End of life, over-pressure, chemical attack

video_tutorials.title: Peristaltic Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Peristaltic Pump.
A peristaltic (hose) pump moves liquid by squeezing a flexible hose or tube with rollers or shoes on a rotor.
The occlusion travels along the hose, pushing the liquid ahead of it; the hose recovers its shape behind the shoe and draws in more liquid.
The liquid touches only the hose.

Typical applications include abrasive slurries and lime milk; chemical dosing (sodium hypochlorite, ferric chloride); mining and alumina: thickener underflow sampling, reagent dosing; food, pharma and lab.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Pump Housing (Lubricant-Filled), Front Cover with Inspection Window, Inlet & Outlet Port Flanges (Hose Clamps), Rotor with Pressing Shoes.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Peristaltic Pump works.
A shoe on the rotor squeezes the hose closed.
As the rotor turns, the occlusion moves along the hose and pushes liquid out.
The hose springs back behind the shoe, creating suction.
The housing is part-filled with lubricant to reduce hose wear and heat.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Peristaltic Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Peristaltic Pump.
Check for hose leakage (leak detector).
Change hose at planned intervals.
Inspect shoes and bearings.
Watch for hose rupture: leak alarm. Common cause: end of life, over-pressure, chemical attack.
Watch for overheating: hot housing. Common cause: high speed, low lubricant.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
